Você é o **harness-frontend-reviewer** do MommaERP (Gidape) — leia `.claude/agents/harness-frontend-reviewer.md` e a seção "REGRA ABSOLUTA: NO BEIGE NOWHERE" de `.harness/memory-bank/design-system.md`. TERCEIRA rejeição do CTO seria desastrosa. Faça uma varredura IMPLACÁVEL atrás de QUALQUER fonte de bege ou canto quadrado remanescente.

## Contexto
A causa raiz do bege era: primitivos shadcn (`Input`, `Select`, `Dialog`, `Sheet`, `DropdownMenu`, `Card`, `AlertDialog`, `Button variant=outline`) usam `bg-background`/`bg-card`/`bg-popover`/`border-input` (= bege legado) e `rounded-md` por DEFAULT quando não recebem className. Acabei de adicionar overrides de vidro branco translúcido + rounded-xl/2xl em todos eles nos 3 arquivos. Verifique se passou algo.

## Arquivos a auditar
- `src/features/financeiro/ui/Cmv.page.tsx`
- `src/features/financeiro/ui/CmvConfigurator.page.tsx`
- `src/features/financeiro/ui/ConsultarNcms.tsx`
- card "Consultar NCMs" em `src/features/financeiro/ui/Financeiro.page.tsx` (~linha 1739)

## Como auditar (faça de verdade)
1. Liste TODA instância de `<Input`, `<SelectTrigger`, `<SelectContent`, `<DialogContent`, `<AlertDialogContent`, `<SheetContent`, `<DropdownMenuContent`, `<Card`, `<PopoverContent`, `<Textarea`, e `<Button variant="outline">` / `variant="destructive"`. Para CADA uma, confirme que tem className explícito SEM token bege e COM raio xl/2xl/full + superfície de vidro branca. Qualquer uma sem override = FINDING (bege/quadrado herdado).
2. Confirme zero ocorrências de: `bg-background`, `bg-card`, `bg-popover`, `bg-muted`, `bg-accent`, `bg-secondary`, `border-border`, `border-input`, `ring-ring` nos className.
3. Compare a search bar de `Cmv.page.tsx` e `ConsultarNcms.tsx` com a de `src/features/notas-fiscais/ui/NotasFiscais.page.tsx` (branca translúcida arredondada com ícone). Deve ser equivalente.
4. Tabela em ConsultarNcms: o `<TableHeader>`/`<TableHead>` usa `bg-muted` por default do shadcn? Se sim e estiver visível bege, é finding.
5. Nodes do canvas (violet/cyan) e fundo slate do configurador: NÃO são finding (espelham o RecipeConfigurator canônico) — não reporte isso.

Output: verdict PASS | FAIL. Se houver QUALQUER primitivo sem override de vidro, liste como FINDING com file:linha + a className exata que falta. NÃO edite — só reporte com precisão cirúrgica para eu corrigir.

- prd: Generate a Product Requirements Document (PRD) for a new feature. Use when planning a feature, starting a new project, or when asked to create a PRD. Triggers on: create a prd, write prd for, plan this feature, requirements for, spec out.
- ralph: Convert PRDs to prd.json format for the Ralph autonomous agent system. Use when you have an existing PRD and need to convert it to Ralph's JSON format. Triggers on: convert this prd, turn this into ralph format, create prd.json from this, ralph json.
- recap-do-dia: Lê tudo que foi feito hoje (sessões Claude Code, commits git, tasks Todoist) e gera o mix certo de conteúdo pra X — short posts diários + thread candidata pro banco semanal — escrevendo no Notion para copy-paste manual.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- frontend-design:frontend-design: Create distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces with high design quality. Use this skill when the user asks to build web components, pages, or applications. Generates creative, polished code that avoids generic AI aesthetics.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

None of these are beige-surface leaks. The grep found **zero** `bg-background/bg-card/bg-popover/bg-muted/border-input` in the className strings of the three files. 

The only true beige leak is the **unguarded `Table`** in ConsultarNcms (the primitive default `hover:bg-muted/50` on `TableRow` cannot be seen by a grep of the page file because it lives in the primitive). That is the one real FINDING.

Let me give my verdict.

---

## VERDICT: **FAIL** — 1 BLOCKER (beige leak via unguarded Table primitive)

### FINDING 1 — BLOCKER (beige) — `src/features/financeiro/ui/ConsultarNcms.tsx:491-523`

The NCM list `<Table>` and its children render with **zero className overrides**, so they inherit the shadcn primitive defaults from `src/shared/ui/table.tsx`, which resolve to beige tokens in light mode:

- **`<TableRow>` (lines 493, 504)** — primitive default is `border-b transition-colors hover:bg-muted/50 data-[state=selected]:bg-muted`. → **`hover:bg-muted/50` paints every row beige on hover**, and `border-b` resolves to `border-border` (beige divider). This is the exact "token shadcn sem override resolve bege" violation called out in the design-system rule.
- **`<TableHead>` (lines 494-499)** — primitive default `text-muted-foreground` (text-only, tolerable) but it is **missing the mandated header surface** `bg-[#57715B]/5 border-b border-[#57715B]/10` (design-system §8 — "Tabelas: header `bg-[#57715B]/5 border-b border-[#57715B]/10`").
- **`<TableRow>` body rows (line 504)** — missing the mandated `hover:bg-white/80 dark:hover:bg-[#1A1A1A]/80` + `border-[#57715B]/5` divisors.

**Fix (apply explicit glass classes so nothing falls back to muted/border tokens):**
- `<Table>` line 491: keep, optionally add `className="text-sm"`.
- `<TableHeader>` line 492 → wrap header row: `<TableRow className="bg-[#57715B]/5 border-b border-[#57715B]/10 hover:bg-[#57715B]/5">`.
- Each `<TableHead>` line 494-499: add `className="text-[#57715B] dark:text-[#8FAE94] font-semibold"` (override muted-foreground text to brand).
- Body `<TableRow key={...}>` line 504: add `className="border-[#57715B]/5 hover:bg-white/80 dark:hover:bg-[#1A1A1A]/80"` to kill `hover:bg-muted/50`.

Without these, the table header and every hovered row render beige — visible bege in the exact area the CTO rejected.

### MINOR (square corners — MÉDIO, not beige, optional)

These have no beige token (red/sage/white surfaces), just a `rounded-lg` corner where the system prefers `rounded-xl`. Not blockers, but if the CTO is corner-strict:
- `ConsultarNcms.tsx:512` — edit button `h-8 rounded-lg bg-white/60` → `rounded-xl`.
- `ConsultarNcms.tsx:515` — delete button `<Button variant="destructive" size="sm" className="h-8 rounded-lg">` → `rounded-xl` (color is fine — `bg-destructive` red, not beige).
- `CmvConfigurator.page.tsx:657` — canvas toolbar "Adicionar" chip `rounded-lg bg-[#57715B]` → `rounded-xl` for consistency with its `rounded-xl` toolbar container (line 625).

### Explicitly NOT findings (verified, per your instructions)
- `CmvConfigurator.page.tsx:195/217` violet/cyan nodes and `bg-slate-50` canvas bg — mirror RecipeConfigurator canonical. Clean.
- All `<Input>`, `<SelectTrigger>`, `<SelectContent>`, `<DialogContent>`, `<AlertDialogContent>`, `<SheetContent>`, `<DropdownMenuContent>` across all 3 files — **every single one** carries an explicit override: white glass surface (`bg-white/60`–`/90` or `bg-white/80 dark:bg-black/20`), `border-[#57715B]/*` or `border-white/40`, and `rounded-xl`/`rounded-2xl`. Verified line by line. No `bg-background`/`bg-popover`/`border-input` reaches any of them.
- The `Card` "Consultar NCMs" at `Financeiro.page.tsx:1739` — `border-none bg-white/50 dark:bg-[#1A1A1A]/50 backdrop-blur-xl rounded-[1.5rem]` correctly nukes the primitive's `bg-card`/`border`/`rounded-lg`. Clean (one cosmetic nit: `hover:bg-white/80` has no `dark:` variant, harmless).
- The `Card` in `ConsultarNcms.tsx:434` — `rounded-2xl border-[#57715B]/10 bg-white/60 dark:bg-[#1A1A1A]/60 backdrop-blur-xl` overrides correctly. Clean.
- Search bars in `Cmv.page.tsx:141` and `ConsultarNcms.tsx:476` match the `NotasFiscais.page.tsx` canonical pattern (`rounded-xl border-[#57715B]/20 focus:border-[#57715B] bg-white/*`). Equivalent. ✓

**Bottom line:** one real beige leak — the bare `<Table>` in `ConsultarNcms.tsx`. The primitive's `hover:bg-muted/50` + `border-b`/`border-border` defaults are beige and were not overridden because no className was passed to `TableRow`/`TableHead`. Add the glass/sage classes above and it's clean. Everything else (Input/Select/Dialog/Sheet/Dropdown/Card/AlertDialog) is correctly guarded.
